# BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation for Large Language Models via Lens of Dynamic Interactions

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#bird-interact)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.05318v3) · arXiv v3, 24 March 2026; ICLR 2026 conference paper

**Reading coverage:** All 49 PDF pages: Sections 1-9, ethics/reproducibility, Appendices A-R, annotation taxonomies, metrics and executable-test examples, simulator design/evaluation and every prompt. Read extracted tables and figure captions; no claim of independently reproducing plotted trajectories.

## Research question

Static dialogue benchmarks cannot measure an agent choosing what to ask, retrieve or execute when user intent, documentation and database state interact.

## Method

BIRD-Interact injects recoverable ambiguities into database tasks and adds dependent follow-ups. A function-driven simulator maps requests to annotated clarification, SQL-fragment localization or refusal. Conversational and autonomous protocols impose different action budgets and test executable outcomes.

## Evaluation

The Full and Lite sets contain 600 and 300 tasks. Seven systems are evaluated per setting in single runs; follow-up success is cumulative. UserSim-Guard tests 2,100 simulator requests. Human alignment compares seven model-level success rates on 100 sampled tasks; dataset-quality review samples 300 items.

## What the results support

Full-set end-to-end agent success reaches 17% for GPT-5. Function-driven simulation improves refusal of inappropriate information requests; GPT-4o simulator scores correlate 0.84 with human-derived model success rates. Additional interaction helps some models, rather than establishing a universal scaling law.

## Limits and qualifications

Unique SQL-grounded clarifications, artificial action costs and expert users constrain realism. UNA concerns privileged or out-of-scope simulator requests, not unanswerable database tasks. Single runs lack variability estimates; finite execution tests do not prove SQL equivalence. Follow-up rates include prior failures.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a controlled environment for source selection, clarification chains and changing database state, with explicit simulator and evaluation boundaries.
